cadence: weekly, Monday before the US open
method: Every Monday each open call is re-examined against the claims its note made. The numbers are computed from the record: where the call stands against what the note called for, how far the stop is, and a price-only range for where it can finish, drawn from the position's own recent volatility with no view assumed. The verdict is a judgment, stated with dated evidence: each claim the note relied on is re-measured and marked as holding or not, and the verdict has to follow from those marks. A broken thesis closes the call on the Scorecard from the review date. The return a note called for is written once and never changed.

latest.book_now: After this week's review the book holds four calls and all four reasons are still in place: long US natural gas, short wheat through the fund, long the yen, and, new this week, long US energy stocks. The energy and natural gas calls share one backdrop, expensive oil and high bond yields, and both readings held through Friday; wheat and the yen stand on their own. Highest conviction remains wheat, which has already earned slightly more than the note called for with the price below its target, followed by natural gas, which has also passed what its note called for and still has a record fund short behind it. Lowest conviction is the yen, three weeks in and flat while the authorities stay quiet, and the energy call, which is only two sessions old and pays one-to-one. A reader holding the calls changes nothing today; this week's test for the energy call is Wednesday's inflation report, which needs to keep bond yields high.

book_risk.note: correlations are of daily mark changes over the trailing 63 sessions; exposure is the position's % move per 1% in equities or the dollar and per +10bp in the 10-year yield

calls.title: The last buyers just showed up in wheat
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate between its one-month (−5.3%) and three-month (−6.6%) medians for a two-month horizon, taken as a short return
calls.expected_basis: the gain to Friday's close (about +7.8% on the short) less a little give-back, with no further drift added because the fund selling the note relied on is done
calls.view_now: The call has done what it said: wheat is at 671, through the note's 685 target, and the fund the reader shorts is down about 8% from entry to Friday. Funds have finished selling out of their record length and have not come back in. Most of the edge is earned, so we expect the call to finish around where it is, a little above what the note called for.
calls.action_reason: Driver intact, target reached, stop far away. It runs to its early-November horizon; the review will close it early if funds start buying wheat back.

calls.expected_basis: the gas fund's gain to Friday's close (about +8.3%) with no further drift added, because the ratio is no longer at the extreme the base rate was measured from; the record fund short is a risk to the upside, not a number we add
calls.view_now: Gas is above the note's 3.05 target and the gap to oil has narrowed from an extreme, as the note said it would. The Scorecard now marks the gas fund a reader actually holds, which has gained about 8% to Friday against the 7.6% the note called for. The fund short in gas is still at a record and has not started to cover, which leaves room for more; we expect the call to finish around where it is now.
calls.action_reason: Driver intact and the stop is far away. It runs to its December horizon; the review will close it early if the ratio swings back toward oil or the fund short is bought back.

calls.title: The record yen rescue looks dead. So did the last three at exactly this point.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's target: 147 on dollar-yen by late January 2027, the median months-two-to-six move applied from 157.34, roughly +6% on the fund
calls.expected_basis: the note's months-two-to-six median move applied from Friday's 158.06, less the small loss so far, cut by about a point because the authorities have been silent for two weeks and the record rests on three episodes
calls.view_now: Three weeks in and flat, which is still what month two looked like in the prior campaigns. The authorities have not acted or spoken again since late September, and the dollar has edged up against the yen, so the call is waiting on them. We still expect the move, but with slightly less time for it and only three prior episodes behind it, we expect a little less than the note called for.
calls.action_reason: The driver is in place and the stop is well away; a flat month two is what the pattern expects. The review will weaken the call if the authorities step back from their readiness to act or dollar-yen pushes toward 162 without a response.

calls.title: Yields and oil are surging together. Energy stocks gained after that in 7 of 8 cases.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return: the average fund return over six months in the eight earlier cases, with the 10% weekly-close exit applied
calls.expected_basis: the note's base rate unchanged, because both conditions read the same as at publication, plus the small loss so far (about -0.2% at Friday's close)
calls.view_now: Two sessions in, both halves of the signal are still in place: oil is near the top of its three-year range and the 10-year yield is just under its high for the year. The fund is flat from entry, which says nothing yet; in the earlier cases it usually fell about 8% before finishing higher. We still expect the call to pan out roughly as the note said.
calls.action_reason: Every condition holds and the exit is about 10% below the market. Wednesday's inflation report is the first test: a soft number that pulls the 10-year yield below 4.75% would weaken the call.
